items.title: CVE-2026-68820: Windows WinSock Zero-Day Exploited by North Korea in Operation Dream Job
items.summary: Microsoft's August 2026 Patch Tuesday patched a use-after-free vulnerability in the Windows Ancillary Function Driver for WinSock (afd.sys). Check Point researchers confirmed North Korean threat actors exploited this zero-day to deploy a kernel-mode rootkit, gaining SYSTEM privileges on targeted systems.
items.why: Actively exploited zero-day by a state-sponsored North Korean APT deploying a kernel-mode rootkit as part of the ongoing Operation Dream Job campaign. Patched as part of Microsoft's August 2026 Patch Tuesday covering 400+ flaws.

items.title: CVE-2026-20127: Cisco SD-WAN Critical Auth Bypass Triggers CISA Emergency Directive 26-03
items.summary: A maximum-severity authentication bypass in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller allows remote unauthenticated attackers to log in as high-privileged users and modify fabric configuration. CISA issued Emergency Directive 26-03 following widespread exploitation with observed webshell deployment activity in the wild.
items.why: Max-severity CVE in widely-deployed enterprise SD-WAN infrastructure with confirmed webshell deployments and a CISA Emergency Directive — the highest-urgency federal response mechanism — demanding immediate patching.

items.title: Salt Typhoon (China APT) Compromises Networks in 80+ Countries Including Telecom and Government
items.summary: China-linked APT Salt Typhoon has dramatically expanded its cyber espionage operations in 2026, compromising networks across more than 80 countries spanning telecommunications, transportation, and government sectors in what analysts are calling one of the most geographically widespread APT campaigns ever documented.
items.why: Unprecedented scale from a China-linked nation-state APT hitting critical infrastructure globally. The breadth — 80+ countries including telecom and government — indicates a strategic intelligence collection operation of historic proportions.

items.title: Iranian APT 'Screening Serpens' Escalates Espionage Operations Across Five Countries with New RAT Families
items.summary: Palo Alto Unit 42 is tracking Iran-nexus group Screening Serpens, which significantly ramped up operations following a regional conflict starting in February 2026. The group is deploying two newly discovered RAT malware families across entities in up to five countries in active espionage campaigns.
items.why: State-sponsored Iranian APT deploying novel, previously undocumented malware families in an escalating campaign directly tied to an active geopolitical conflict — conflict-driven APT escalation is a reliable indicator of intensifying offensive operations.

items.title: CrowdStrike 2026 Global Threat Report: AI-Accelerated Attacks Up 89%, Adversary Breakout Time Drops to 29 Minutes
items.summary: CrowdStrike's 2026 Global Threat Report documents an 89% surge in AI-enabled cyberattacks with adversary breakout times shrinking to just 29 minutes on average. China-nexus actors are weaponizing critical CVEs within 24 hours of PoC publication, and cloud-related eCrime surged 171% driven by credential theft, LLM abuse, and cryptomining.
items.why: 29-minute average breakout time means defenders have an ever-narrowing window for detection and response. The 89% AI-attack increase and same-day CVE weaponization by nation-state actors are inflection points that demand updated defensive postures and faster patch cycles.
